root.name: Zukertort Opening: Double Fianchetto Attack
root.moves: 1. Nf3 Nf6 2. g3 g6 3. b3 Bg7 4. Bb2 O-O 5. Bg2 d6 6. O-O

overview: Both sides develop with g3/Bg2, b3/Bb2 and castle, with Black in a King's Indian-style fianchetto set-up. White keeps the centre flexible and plans d3/c4 and e4 or d4, aiming for a slow squeeze on the long diagonals. Play is quiet and manoeuvring, with few early tactics.

white_ideas.idea: Use the b2 and g2 bishops along the long diagonals
Prepare c4 and d4 or e4 for a central break

black_ideas.idea: Mirror with ...Bg7 and ...d6 and prepare ...e5 or ...c5
Fight for the centre with ...Nc6 and ...e5

typical_structures.structure: Hypermodern double fianchetto with an undecided centre

character.notes: Quiet fianchetto play where neither side has an easy target, so it is hard to lose quickly.

structure.notes: The centre is left undecided for a long time.

approach.notes: A set-up White can play against almost any reply, closely related to the King's Indian Attack.

level.notes: Clear piece placement with little theory, but subtle plans.
